title: Open Legend — Final Creative Inspiration Board
status: Confirmed favorites; proposed translation into Open Legend, not a locked production pipeline

entries.title: Dave the Diver
entries.liked: Your strongest new endorsement: “I LOVE DAVE THE DIVER ART.” You supplied the underwater scene, character close-up and restaurant as references.
entries.good: The underwater image pairs a small readable diver with enormous layered rock forms, blue atmospheric depth and delicate coral. The chef close-up describes face, fabric folds and a purposeful gesture. In the restaurant, varied bodies and outfits make a busy social scene feel inhabited.
entries.apply: Give the wilderness depth and breathing room; make individuals recognizable through body shape, hair, skin tone and equipment. Let closer character views reveal richer faces and material detail while world avatars stay legible.
entries.limit: The chef is a close-up, not evidence of facial detail at gameplay distance. Your new endorsement broadens the earlier concerns about cartoon-like proportions: appealing stylization is welcome when the finish and personality work.

images.label: World scale · clear silhouette, luminous water and layered terrain
Close-up · expressive anatomy, clothing folds and purposeful action
Social scale · distinctive people, inhabited detail and warm lighting

entries.title: Steam Autumn Sale illustration
entries.liked: You called this exceptional, specifically praising pixel density and character/environment detail.
entries.good: Twisting foreground roots, layered buildings, little storefront objects and differentiated figures make the scene reward close inspection. The brightest shop holds attention; quieter blue silhouettes keep the density organized. Reflections connect the lights to the ground.
entries.apply: Use deliberate fine detail for clothing, tools, bark, shelters and small possessions. Compose scenes with foreground framing, readable figures and a clear focal area. A dense world should still have quiet spaces.
entries.limit: This is a promotional illustration, not a game. It establishes a visual aspiration, not evidence of runtime performance, animation or procedural generation. Artist and original publication provenance are not verified; preserve the supplied screenshot as reference only.

images.label: Full supplied illustration · foreground roots, readable people and layered environmental detail

entries.title: Pathway
entries.liked: You singled out Pathway’s lighting as really great.
entries.good: Amber illumination against blue-violet surroundings models the stone, separates figures and throws long directional shadows. The recruitment view demonstrates a readable world figure paired with a more detailed portrait and equipment display.
entries.apply: Make campfires and lanterns cast convincing pools of color and directional shadows. Carry light onto nearby materials and characters. Use profiles to reveal identity and gear without requiring tiny world faces to do everything.
entries.limit: The supplied image shows the appearance of lighting, not proof of a particular lighting implementation. Borrow the light/material relationship; the historical setting and parchment UI are not selected requirements.

images.label: Warm light / cool shadow · relief in stone and grounded figures
World figure + profile · two useful scales of character information

entries.title: Hades
entries.liked: You explicitly love Hades and call its art really great.
entries.good: Clear silhouettes and strongly grouped color let an ornate angled world remain readable. Vegetation, water and stone each contribute distinct shapes.
entries.apply: Aim for a coherent art direction across people, environment and props; use color grouping to make a rich scene easy to read.
entries.limit: Illustrated rather than conventional pixel art. Its mythology, combat effects and exaggerated character design are not automatically part of our brief.

images.label: Elysium · water, vegetation and gameplay-scale character

entries.title: Hades II
entries.medium: Illustrated hybrid presentation; not pixel art
entries.liked: You explicitly love Hades II and reaffirmed it as a favorite.
entries.good: The small world figures and expressive large portraits serve different jobs. Costumes and silhouettes communicate identity; close views provide face and personality.
entries.apply: Create an intentional relationship between recognizable world agents and detailed character profiles. Let clothing and possessions tell personal stories.
entries.limit: The dialogue reference is Early Access media. A beautiful portrait alone does not establish that ordinary world avatars meet our identity requirements.

images.label: Official Early Access image · portrait versus world avatar

entries.title: REPLACED
entries.liked: REPLACED was your strongest preference in both earlier rounds, and you reaffirm it here.
entries.good: Fine environmental detail, dimensional lighting and carefully staged space create a cinematic finish rather than a deliberately coarse retro one.
entries.apply: Use it as the standard for care in surfaces, clothing, atmosphere and scene composition. Translate that finish into vegetation, wood, stone and primitive possessions.
entries.limit: Some reference imagery is promotional. The city, side-view camera, violence and nighttime mood are not selected requirements; a still does not verify animation.

entries.title: Tails Noir / Backbone
entries.liked: A repeated favorite: you specifically praised water reflections, lighting, character detail and the environment.
entries.good: Readable clothing and dense inhabited surroundings work together. Reflected light ties architecture, water and figures into one convincing place.
entries.apply: Give people distinctive outfits and grounded material responses. Carry atmosphere through the entire scene, not just a background layer.
entries.limit: Borrow the finish, not the anthropomorphic cast, city setting or noir mood as a permanent default.

entries.title: Transistor
entries.liked: You named Transistor among the beautiful games in your final favorites.
entries.good: Repeated shapes, colored light and graphic architectural detail create a unified scene around a distinct protagonist.
entries.apply: Choose purposeful palettes and shapes for each place. Let clothing and important objects stand out without turning every element into a bright accent.
entries.limit: Urban geometry and science fiction are references for composition, not the wilderness subject matter.

images.label: Gameplay · world figure and architectural detail

entries.title: Octopath Traveler II
entries.role: Intimate light in a large world
entries.liked: You now name Octopath Traveler as a favorite. Earlier you especially praised lighting, mood and palette while wanting a more modern treatment of people.
entries.good: Warm campfire light against the cool surrounding wilderness makes a small party feel present and protected. The depth gives the setting scale.
entries.apply: Use firelight, shade and daylight to change the emotional character of a place. Keep a small human gathering readable within expansive nature.
entries.limit: The image is Octopath Traveler II. Miniature figures and strong blur are not mandatory: earlier reservations remain useful component-level guidance.

entries.title: Eastward
entries.role: A place with life in it
entries.liked: You love Eastward’s environment, colors, lighting and mood, and include it in the final favorites. Earlier you asked for more detailed bodies and readable gear.
entries.good: Small props, layered architecture and vegetation make the environment seem used and lived in. Color variety adds warmth without making every object equally important.
entries.apply: Let camps accumulate meaningful objects: bundles, tools, cooking materials, wear and vegetation. Create richness through the traces of people living there.
entries.limit: Liking the whole direction does not require copying its simplified character proportions. Keep clothing and gear legible at our actual camera scale.

entries.title: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
entries.medium: Painterly, dimensional presentation; not pixel art
entries.liked: You named Ori as one of the beautiful final favorites.
entries.good: Organic silhouettes and atmospheric layers create deep space. Light separates surfaces and suggests moisture, air and distance.
entries.apply: Build a wilderness with layered foliage, clear near/far relationships and luminous moments. Let forests feel alive, including in daylight.
entries.limit: Painterly dimensional presentation, not conventional pixel art. The nonhuman protagonist is not a human-character reference. Persistent gloom or heavy blur is not required.

images.label: Forest gameplay · depth and organic materials
